_readme: ชื่อเดียวกันคนละสคริปต์ — which name-words gather a family, and which do not.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Every state register in this catalogue writes Thai and nothing
else (ONAB temples 2,084 · OBEC schools 1,302 · MOPH 490 · OPEC 168 · FDA 907 ·
condominiums 367); 8,676 of the 14,851 OSM records carry a Latin name and no
Thai one. Only 24% of records hold both scripts of their own name. So one place
stands in the directory twice, in two alphabets, and neither half sees the
other — which is how a resident came to say his condominium was not on the site
while ten Punna records sat there.
THE JOIN IS THE READING, NOT A FUZZY MATCH. Fixed at the reading layer instead:
data/curated/rtgs_lexicon.json now carries the building loanwords (ยูนีค is
Unique, not Yu Nik; ฮิลล์ไซด์ is Hillside, not Hinsai) and a `brand` section for
a name's own Latin spelling read off a record in this same catalogue (ปันนา is
Punna, which is painted on three buildings here, not Panna). With the readings
right, families join on the EXACT romanised token and no similarity test is
needed at all: 33 families now hold a register row and a mapped building
together, Punna's ten among them. Every fuzzy rule measured on 2026-09-04 was
refused — the consonant skeleton puts เพนนี Penny Place among the Punnas, one
edit chains ahan→akhan→akhin→anan, and the strict one-vowel test still merges
chai with chao. importers/audit_name_families.py prints what any of them would
have joined; none of it is applied.
WHAT A FAMILY IS NOT. It says two names share their identifying word. It does
NOT say two records are one place — that is merges.json — and it does NOT say
one company owns them: nothing on this disk states who developed Punna.
`generic` is the refusal list: words that name a KIND or a PLACE rather than a
building, so a family keyed on them gathers strangers. Three grounds, and every
entry says which. Roads and districts already have their own pages; a family
keyed on a toponym would be a worse copy of one.

generic.ying: kind — หญิง, the sex of a dormitory: 13 unrelated หอ N หญิง
generic.chai: kind — ชาย on the dorms, and it also catches ชัย/ชายน์ in real names
generic.satri: kind — สตรี, women's dormitory
generic.flaet: kind — แฟลต, a flat block
generic.khrongkan: kind — โครงการ, 'project N' of a named development
generic.akhan: kind — อาคาร, the word building itself
generic.chaonathi: kind — เจ้าหน้าที่, staff housing
generic.kamkap: kind — ในกำกับ, a university-supervised hall
generic.condotel: kind — the trade word, worn by any of them
generic.retsiden: kind — a variant spelling of เรสซิเดนซ์ the lexicon now reads
generic.hill: descriptor — any building on a slope may wear it
generic.suan: descriptor — สวน, garden, in บ้านสวน and a dozen unrelated names
generic.chang: toponym — ช้างคลาน and ช้างเผือก are two different districts
generic.huai: toponym — ห้วย, the stream in a hundred road names
generic.nakhon: toponym — นคร, in นครพิงค์ and ลานนานคร, which are not one family
generic.ping: toponym — the river, and พิงค์ is also a brand's own word; ambiguous, so refused until a person separates them

unions.why: REFUSED, kept as the record of a refusal. ชัย and เชา are different words; the one-vowel test cannot tell them apart, which is why no similarity test publishes here.

REFUSED. เพนนี Penny Place is not a Punna building. Both reduce to the consonant skeleton pn, which is why the skeleton is a sweep and never a join. Punna itself needs no union any more: the lexicon reads ปันนา as Punna.
